body:
Thanks for the info and examples, definitely helpful. 

Just so I'm understanding your suggestion:
- Basically each category results component will be wrapped in `connectInfiniteHits`. 
- After a user types in a query in the search field and clicks "show more results" for a specific category, it will hide the other category results components via a state change in `SiteSearch` (`viewShowMore`) and only show the targeted category results component with the "Load More" button.
- Clicking on the "Back to all results", will re-show all of the all category results components, hide the "Load More" button, and all `searchState` values will persist through all of these views and interactions.

A few questions:
* Since the `page` key-value affect which/how many results show in each category, will this get reset back to `0` if a user clicks "Load more" at least once in the "show more" view and then clicks "back to results"? We want to always show the first 5 results in each category in the "All Results" view.
* How can I hide the "Load more" button in the category results component while in the "All Results" view and then show it while in the "ShowMoreResults" view? Ideally, I could do this via passing in the "viewShowMore" state value from `SiteSearch` down to these category results components via a prop and then choose to show or hide it.
* In your proposal, will I still be able to maintain the exact same UI behavior as in the GIF I posted earlier? In order to get the sliding affect, I would have to position that "show more" category results component offscreen on "viewShowMore" state change and then slide it in, but I'd have to test to see if there will be any jumpiness in the UI.

Let me about the above and maybe I'll test out your suggestions to see if I can get this working.
